name: devshell-init
what_it_does: Adds a pinned set of development tools to a repo, so the same versions appear on every machine that opens it.
what_you_say: set this project up with its own toolchain
what_you_get: Three files in your repo (`flake.nix`, `.envrc`, `CLAUDE.md`), and the output of the check that the right tools are now in use.
on_your_computer: Writes those three files into the repo you name, then downloads and switches on a Nix toolchain. The tools switch on again each time you enter that folder. Needs Nix and direnv.

name: new-project
what_it_does: Interviews you about a new project, then creates the folder, the git setup, a secret scan on every commit, a licence and the four project documents.
what_you_say: start a new repo for a python pipeline
what_you_get: A new project folder with a first commit of setup only, four written documents, and, when you run the publish step, a GitHub repository with that commit pushed.
on_your_computer: Creates a new folder, by default under your home folder at `~/work/GitHub/<name>`, runs the bundled setup script, and on the publish step creates a real GitHub repository under your account and pushes to it. Needs `git`, `gh`, `gitleaks` and `pre-commit`.

name: pipeline-foundry
what_it_does: Turns a project idea into a brief a fresh Claude Code session can execute from, settling scope, decision authority and what counts as done.
what_you_say: turn this idea into a handoff a fresh session can run
what_you_get: A zip of project documents, or a named blocker and the advice to shelve the project if a readiness check fails.
on_your_computer: Reads templates from a local copy of the `gfm-foundry` project and writes the documents into a zip for you. It recommends a weekly cloud job that works on the project unattended.

name: project-kb-builder
what_it_does: Breaks one long reference document into a set of topic-sized markdown files a Claude Project can look answers up in.
what_you_say: turn this 100-page PDF into knowledge files for a project
what_you_get: A numbered set of markdown files, an index file first, with source contradictions flagged rather than smoothed over.
on_your_computer: Reads the document you give it and writes markdown files. It was written for the Claude website and writes to `/mnt/user-data/outputs/`, which does not exist in Claude Code, so that step needs a local folder instead.

name: project-setup-wizard
what_it_does: Takes a rough brain dump about something you are starting and turns it into a project description and a set of instructions for Claude.
what_you_say: /newproject or "help me set up a project for this"
what_you_get: Three blocks of text to copy: a project description, a setup summary with documents to upload, and a full set of project instructions.

name: systems-design
what_it_does: Runs a guided conversation that works backwards from the outcome you want, maps what must be true at each stage, and tests it against how it could fail.
what_you_say: help me work backwards from this goal
what_you_get: A summary document with the end state, the dependency map, ranked failure modes and sprint-sized blocks, plus a diagram of the system.
on_your_computer: Runs a conversation of 20 to 30 minutes, then saves one document and draws one diagram. It was written for the Claude website: the output path, the question tool and the file viewer it names are not present in Claude Code.
